models.collectorNote: Spyder conversions pollute the market — verify against factory records. A documented SS coupé is the blue-chip Maserati of the era.

generations.name: Ghibli / Ghibli SS
generations.note: Dry-sump V8, pop-up lamps, and steel or alloy bodies. Faster in a straight line than a Daytona, more relaxed everywhere else — the connoisseur's Italian GT.

models.intro: Giugiaro's masterpiece for Ghia: a long-bonnet GT with a quad-cam V8 and the longest, lowest silhouette of its era. The SS with the 4.9 is the one that matters.
models.name: Ghibli (AM115)

models.collectorNote: Depreciation did the first owners no favours and buyers every favour. Trofeos are rare and holding; V6 cars want timing-chain and service-history scrutiny.

generations.name: Ghibli / Trofeo
generations.note: Chrysler-era platform, Ferrari F160 V6 built in Maranello, and ZF eight-speed. The 2020 Trofeo added the F154 V8 and a Corsa mode — the last V8 Maserati sedan.

models.intro: The modern Ghibli took the fight to the 5 Series with Ferrari-built twin-turbo engines and proper Italian drama. The Trofeo's 580 hp V8 made it a Q-car of the first order.
models.name: Ghibli (M157)

generations.name: Quattroporte I
generations.note: Frua styling, a 260 hp V8 from the 450S racing programme's family, and 170+ mph ambitions in a limousine body. The car that invented the genre AMG now owns.

generations.name: Quattroporte VI
generations.note: The final Quattroporte: Ghibli's bigger brother with a Ferrari-built 3.8 V8 in the GTS and Trofeo. Ended in 2024 with the Ultima celebrations.

models.intro: The original sports saloon: Maserati put racing V8s in four-door bodies in 1963 and kept the nameplate alive for six generations until 2024.
models.name: Quattroporte

generations.name: GranTurismo
generations.note: The 4.7 in the S and MC Stradale is the soundtrack car — one of the great production V8 exhaust notes, wrapped in the era's prettiest coupé body.

generations.name: GranTurismo Modena / Folgore
generations.note: One body, two cars: the Nettuno twin-turbo V6 (542 hp in Trofeo form) or the tri-motor Folgore EV with 800-volt architecture and 751 hp.

models.intro: Pininfarina's long-lived GT defined Maserati for a decade with a Ferrari V8; the second generation returned in 2023 with the Nettuno V6 and an all-electric Folgore flagship.
models.name: GranTurismo

photos.credit: Photo: Calreyn88, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

models.collectorNote: Fifty cars and no casual market — MC12s lead Maserati values at auction, and provenance documentation is the entire conversation.

generations.name: MC12 Stradale
generations.note: 50 road cars, all in white over blue. The race Corsa took the longer nose, the wins, and the mythology.

models.intro: Maserati's return to racing, built on the Enzo's bones to homologate a GT1 car. Bigger, rarer, and in race trim far more successful than the Ferrari it came from — five FIA GT titles.
models.name: MC12

generations.name: MC20 / Cielo
generations.note: 621 hp from 3.0 litres, a Dallara-developed tub at 1,500 kg, and no hybrid hardware. The Cielo spyder adds a retractable glass roof; the GT2 Stradale sharpens it for the road.

models.intro: The Trident's clean-sheet supercar: a carbon tub, butterfly doors, and the Nettuno V6 with F1-style pre-chamber ignition — Maserati's own engine again, at last.
models.name: MC20
